title: Latency isochrones & hotspot catalog
content:
Purpose and scope:
Quick working catalog of latency isochrones and hotspot patterns we observed in the last three weeks of sampling. This is a hybrid note: part lab notebook (raw traces + hypotheses), part playbook fragment for follow-ups. Intention is to capture reproducible signatures (isochrones) and short textual fingerprints we can match against future regressions.

Executive summary (short):
- Stable p50 but noisy p95/p99 across traffic mixes.
- Dominant p99 contributors: batcher queuing spikes (cold cohorts), a subset of long-sequence kernel paths, and occasional KV miss cascades that amplify batch wait.
- We can reduce observed p99 by ~35–50% for common customer cohorts via three low-risk changes: (1) aggressive per-route batch caps, (2) KV prefetch for hotPrefix cohorts, (3) kernel slow-path mitigation for >512 token decode.

Representative overall E2E quantiles (control run: 2024-10-09, region us-west-2, g4dn cluster):
- E2E p50: 42 ms
- E2E p95: 210 ms
- E2E p99: 1,320 ms
Notes: numbers are from sampled traces filtered to 10k requests/min baseline traffic; see linked trace set for raw spans.

Per-stage breakdown (median/p95/p99 ms) — canonical stages we tag in traces:
- Ingress (LB + TLS): 3 / 7 / 20
- Auth & quota eval: 2 / 6 / 60
- Router/policy eval: 4 / 12 / 150
- Batcher wait (per-batch enqueue -> dispatch): 8 / 40 / 700
- KV cache lookup (prefix + embedding cache): 1 / 5 / 120 (misses spike to 120+ ms when remote lookup triggered)
- Model runtime (kernel + decode): 20 / 120 / 400 (highly seq-len dependent)
- Emit & streaming setup: 2 / 10 / 80
- Egress + client ack: 2 / 5 / 20

Observations and pattern fingerprints (isochrones/hotspots):
1) Batcher Isochrone: the p99 tail aligns tightly with long enqueue times (batch wait) rather than model kernel time. Isochrone signature: a sudden vertical spread in per-token timestamps starting at "batcher.enqueue" and ending at "batcher.dispatch" — typically 200–900 ms. Cohort: bursty traffic with mixed seq-len where small requests are being held to fill large-target batches.

2) KV-miss cascade: multiple sequential requests hitting the same cold prefix will cause repeated remote KV lookups; the trace shows repeated ~100–180 ms spikes in KV lookup spans, chained closely with extra batching delay as cache-miss requests wait for remote resolution. Fingerprint: repeated KV remote spans + increased batcher wait for the same route id.

3) Long-seq kernel slow-path: any request with decode length >512 tokens occasionally triggers a fallback kernel (unquantized path) which multiplies runtime by ~2–3x. Signature: model.runtime kernel span large AND consistent per-token emission time increase; heatmap shows longer per-token intervals. These are rare but dominate p99 when they occur.

4) Router policy blocking (intermittent): rare (p99 contributors) spikes connected to policy-store timeouts (config service). Signature: router.policy eval span jumps to 100–300ms; often correlated with config refresh jitter.

Cohort breakdown (sampled):
- Small prompts (<64 tokens): E2E p50=35ms, p95=95ms, p99=450ms. Major tail cause: batcher wait.
- Medium prompts (64–256): E2E p50=52ms, p95=220ms, p99=780ms. Mix of batcher wait + kernel variability.
- Long prompts (>512): E2E p50=180ms, p95=620ms, p99=1,800ms. Kernel slow-paths and memory churn.

Cold vs Warm cache behavior:
- Warm KV cache: KV span median ~1ms, negligible effect on p95.
- Cold KV lookup: median ~120ms; when 1% of requests are KV-miss, p99 increases ~300–500ms due to queuing ripple. Recommendation: pre-warm first-token prefixes for heavy routes.

Hypotheses (ranked):
H1 (high impact, high probability): Batcher waiting policy (max_batch_wait + shape heuristic) is allowing long-tail amplification when traffic mixes short and long seq requests. Reducing the max wait for routes serving predominantly short prompts should collapse p99 dramatically.
H2 (medium): KV miss cascades are amplifying the batcher effect for certain prefixes. Prefetch/hotset caching will mitigate.
H3 (low): Kernel selection occasionally picks a slow codepath for certain model shims; this is triggered by internal quantization flags when sequence length >512. Fixing selection logic yields improvement for long requests.
H4 (rare): Router policy store timeouts correlate to config refresh windows — operational, fixable by retry/backoff.

Quick experiments run (results):
- EXP-2024-10-BATCHCAP: Per-route batch cap (cap batches to 8 for route "assistant-lite") reduced p99 for that route from ~920ms to ~360ms; E2E p95 improved ~25%. Traces: linked PR and trace id.
- EXP-2024-10-KV-PREFETCH: Prefetching top-1 hotPrefix reduced KV miss rate from 1.1% -> 0.12% for test traffic; p99 down 180ms on average for related cohort.
- EXP-2024-11-KERNEL-FLAKE: Reproduced a kernel slow-path with an instrumented microbench; created issue and small patch (PR reference included). Effect: ~40% reduction in median for >512 cohort in microbench, needs canary.

Playbook / immediate mitigations (low-risk):
1) Deploy per-route batch caps for high-short-request routes (owner: Ravi, ETA: 2024-11-05).
2) Enable KV hot-prefix prefetch for top 50 routes (owner: Maya, ETA: 2024-11-12).
3) Canary kernel selection patch on a small dedicated shard (owner: Ethan, ETA: 2024-11-18).
4) Add trace alert rule: if p99 grows by >200ms and batcher.wait accounts for >40% of E2E tail, page on-call (SRE).

Data collection notes / instrumentation gaps:
- Need better per-token timestamps exported from kernel path for all model types (not all backends include per-token emit spans). Action: add per-token emit marker at the runtime boundary.
- Traces sometimes lack route metadata when routed through legacy LB; we should enforce route tagging at ingress.

Open action items (short):
- [Avery] finalize batch cap rollout plan + add metric to dashboard (due 2024-10-20).
- [Ravi] create feature flag for per-route batch cap (INF-2410).
- [Maya] instrument KV-prefetch telemetry + list of hot prefixes (due 2024-10-28).
- [Ethan] push kernel selection patch to canary and run compare traces (due 2024-11-18).

Notes to self / rough TODOs (informal):
- When reproducing, prefer uniform qps spike generator with mixed seq-len seed to stress batching heuristics.
- Capture a run with disabled adaptive batching to see baseline microburst behavior.
- Check GPU scheduling logs around times of the largest p99 runs — are we seeing slot churn?

Appendix: quick checklist to reproduce a representative p99 run locally in perf cluster:
1) Use loadgen with 80% short (<64) + 20% long (>512) mix at 10k rps.
2) Route all traffic to a single serving pod with batcher enabled (max batch size 32, max wait 30ms).
3) Enable full tracing and record 10k traces.
4) Run trace classifier (script path in repo) to extract isochrones and batcher span distributions.

If anything needs to be forked into a more formal postmortem / opt plan, call it out and I will convert. For now this lives as working catalog and playbook for follow-ups.

-- Avery

Raw references and quick links: see linked_artifacts above (confluence + jira + PR + trace).
